_why: What must be TRUE on the live host after a deploy — the half that closes 'shipped is not verified'.
Read by scripts/predeploy-check.mjs --live, which runs automatically as the last step of npm run deploy:home.
Each marker is a string that only appears if the page actually rendered its own content, so a page that
deployed-but-did-not-land fails loudly instead of returning a cheerful 200. Pick markers that would DISAPPEAR
if the thing broke: a heading the page owns, an element id its script fills, a function name in a module.
A marker that can never fail is worse than no marker — it buys false confidence. Add a page here the same
day you add it to public/, or it ships unwatched.
NOTE: signed-in surfaces cannot be asserted from here. /status's Operations section, the runbook documents
and /admin's member table are all injected only after Firebase sign-in, which this unauthenticated fetch
never has. The markers below are therefore the page CHROME and its gate — proof the shell shipped, never
proof the gated content works. That still has to be checked by signing in.
/status is HEALTH now — the front door of the four-page split (2026-08-18, owner: 'maybe a health page
that also has logs for the pods/workers/containers, a page for data processing, a page for running the
pipelines and their logs'). It keeps the two probe lists and the migration runbooks; the run controls
and the ingestion pause card MOVED to /status/pipelines/ and their markers moved with them, to that
page's own entry below. A pin left behind on the old page is worse than no pin: it would fail every
deploy for a control that is working perfectly somewhere else.
The four nav hrefs are pinned as a SET because the shared shell is the thing the split actually added —
a page that lost its nav still serves a cheerful 200 and simply strands the reader on one tab with no
way to reach the other three.
mustNotContain pins the REMOVAL half, per the rework precedent: id=ingestion-card is exactly what a
stale bundle of the pre-split page would still carry while satisfying every marker above.
/status/pipelines — RUN + CONTROL, the page the levers moved to on 2026-08-18. Everything here was
pinned on /status before the split and is pinned here now, unchanged in meaning: the pipeline steps, the
Run levers, and the ingestion pause card.
The ingestion pause card (2026-08-18, owner: 'give me a way to pause and start the process flow on the
GABI dashboard... let me also set pause timers on the ui. I can say don't even check to start until x
time.'). The card's BUTTONS are built by pipelines.js after sign-in and cannot be asserted from here, but
its shell ships in this HTML and every marker below is a piece whose absence would leave a control that
still returns a cheerful 200 while doing nothing: id=ingestion-card is the card, id=ingestion-status and
id=ingestion-headline are where the running/paused sentence lands (a blank there is the exact failure
the card exists to prevent), and the two picker ids are the timers.
'Phoenix time' is asserted as TEXT, not as an element: a datetime-local input with no zone stated is a
control that silently means a different hour on a travelling phone, and that label is the only thing on
the page saying which zone the picker is read in.
pipelines.js (2026-08-18) carries the pause card's LOGIC, moved out of status.js by the split. These
three markers moved with it from the /status/status.js entry below and mean exactly what they meant
there: the route the card reads and writes (a bundle pointing at a route the Worker does not serve would
leave the card permanently unreadable), buildIngestionCard (the four two-tap buttons — without it the
card renders a status line and no controls), and the ingestion-time.js import (the two files must ship
together or the page's script dies at parse time with the usual cheerful 200 on the route).
The pure half's own 23 tests still live in scripts/test/ingestion-time.test.mjs and still pass — the
module did not move, only its caller did.
/status/agents — CLAUDE CAPACITY (2026-08-18). Everything on it is PUSHED, so the markers are the
chrome and the freshness apparatus, never the data.
id=board-fresh is the freshness strip and is the single most important marker on this page: without it a
reader cannot tell a live board from one pushed before lunch, which is the failure the whole page is
designed around. The three mount ids are where the running agents, the event feed and the usage figures
land; a missing one leaves a heading with silence under it.
agents.js (2026-08-18). fetchBoard is the shared reader in status/lib/board.js — its name appearing here
proves the module graph actually shipped, since a missing lib/ file takes the page's script down at
parse time while the route still serves 200.
The three usage keys are the estate's own meters and are pinned because a usage block that silently lost
one would look complete: three tiles is not a shape a reader counts.
/status/processing — DATA PROCESSING (2026-08-18, owner: 'which books are being processed right now,
per-book % progress, a history of everything processed, and next to each processed book a label saying
when it became part of GABI's knowledge base').
⚠ THE HOME-MACHINE PUSHER DOES NOT EXIST YET, so this page's four lists render worded empty states
rather than data. That is precisely why the markers are the mount ids and the owner's own sentence: they
prove the page landed, and they would disappear if a later edit 'tidied away' an empty-looking section.
'Joined GABI's knowledge base' is asserted as TEXT because it is the label he asked for by name.
processing.js (2026-08-18). Same module-graph proof as agents.js (fetchBoard), plus the two renderers
whose absence would leave the page's most-asked-for sections silently blank.
normaliseQueue is pinned because it is the tolerance that lets the unbuilt pusher send either shape of
queue data — losing it in a refactor would make the queue section empty on the day the pipeline
finally ships, which is the worst possible day to discover it.
The shared shell the split created (2026-08-18). status-shell.css is loaded by ALL FOUR pages, so a
failed upload of this one file leaves four unstyled pages serving cheerful 200s. .statusnav is the nav
itself; .freshstrip is the staleness apparatus on the two pushed-data pages; .proc-row and .usage-tile
are the two blocks the split added.
status/lib/ — the three modules every page imports (2026-08-18). Pinned SEPARATELY from the pages
because an ES-module import failure is invisible from the importing page's HTML: the route serves 200,
the script dies at the import, and nothing renders. gate.js is the one that matters most — it is the
single implementation of the devops gate for all four pages, and four copies of a gate is four chances
for one to fail open.
board.js — the shared reader and the freshness sentence for both pushed-data pages.
⚠ sectionFreshness and section_pushed_at (2026-08-18) are the fix for the contract's §9 wrinkle: one
D1 row, two pushers, each writing the board whole, so the board-wide pushed_at only ever said when
SOMEBODY pushed — and /status/agents read 'as of 2 minutes ago' over agent rows hours old. A bundle
that lost these would go back to a strip that says fresh about stale data, which is the one failure a
freshness strip must not have and the one a cheerful 200 would never reveal.
ebook-lane.js (2026-08-18) — the ebook row's VERDICT, extracted from status.js with the FOURTH fix to a
row that had shipped wrong three times. The two markers that used to sit on /status/status.js moved
here WITH the logic, per pins-follow-their-subject: a pin left on the old file fails every deploy for
code that works perfectly one module over, and a pin deleted instead of moved silently stops watching.
ebookLaneVerdict is what the page calls; EBOOK_PRODUCING_TRIGGERS and ebookRunKind are the cross-repo
trigger contract with audiobook_catalog.
⚠ 'ebookCount' is pinned as THE SIGNAL ITSELF. The whole fix is that this row compares the published
shelf COUNT against the count the last run built, instead of comparing timestamps — a refactor that
quietly went back to timestamps would reproduce the exact false amber the owner reported three times.
Its behaviour is pinned by scripts/test/ebook-lane.test.mjs against the live payload that produced it.
storage-view.js (2026-08-18) — the blob-storage panel's WORDS. Pinned separately from status.js for the
usual ES-module reason: a missing lib/ file takes the importing page's script down at parse time while
the route still serves a cheerful 200.
⚠ 'not zero' is pinned as a STRING, not as an identifier, and it is the most important marker here. The
panel's whole contract is that an unmeasured bucket reads as UNKNOWN — a size of '—' and a sentence
saying so — because rendering a bucket nobody could measure as 0 B is, on the BACKUPS bucket, the most
alarming wrong answer this estate could publish. A refactor that dropped that wording would look
perfectly fine on a page where every bucket happened to answer.
ingestion-time.js (2026-08-18) is the PURE half of the pause card — the Phoenix conversion and every
word the card says. Its correctness is pinned by scripts/test/ingestion-time.test.mjs, so these markers
are about the file having actually SHIPPED: status.js imports it, and a missing module takes the whole
page's script down at parse time with the usual cheerful 200 on the route.
'America/Phoenix' and 'midnight tonight' are the two strings whose disappearance would mean the estate's
timezone or the owner's own phrasing had been refactored away.
The Drive ⇄ role parity markers (2026-08-17) pin the row that watches audiobook_catalog pipeline STEP 8 —
the one step in the estate that changes a PERSON'S ACCESS unattended. renderDriveParityRow is the row;
driveParityState is the exact Firestore field it READS (the ebook row above is the standing proof of what
inference costs on this page — three wrong colours); and 'fuse-tripped' is the state that must never
silently vanish, since it is the one saying a mass change was REFUSED and is waiting for a human. A bundle
missing any of the three would still serve a cheerful 200 with the row simply absent.
⚠ THE INGESTION PAUSE CARD'S THREE MARKERS LEFT THIS ENTRY on 2026-08-18 with the /status split — the
card now lives in /status/pipelines/pipelines.js and its pins moved to that file's entry above, intact.
They were NOT deleted: a pin that follows its subject keeps failing for the right reason, while a pin
left on the old file fails every deploy for a control that is working perfectly one page over.
⚠ THE EBOOK LANE'S TWO LOGIC MARKERS LEFT THIS ENTRY on 2026-08-18 for the same reason, one layer
down: ebookRunKind and EBOOK_PRODUCING_TRIGGERS now live in /status/lib/ebook-lane.js and are pinned
on that file's own entry above. renderPipelineEbookRow STAYS here, because the DOM adapter that puts
the verdict on the row is still this file's job — and it is the marker whose absence would mean the
row silently stopped rendering at all.
ebook-lane.js is also pinned as an IMPORT below, so a bundle that shipped this file without its new
dependency fails here rather than dying at parse time behind a cheerful 200.
⚠️ REBUILT 2026-08-17 FOR THE CONTROL-GRAMMAR RESHAPE. Owner order: 'auth setting has too many
different auth setting experiences, sometimes we double click to confirm sometimes we use the drop
down. also at the top we have a tree for audio and ebooks but not one for the other sites. maybe just
make a full permission map after normalizing everything.' The member table is signed-in-only, but
every structural piece of that reshape ships in the HTML and IS assertable unauthenticated: the
grammar in the (owner-trimmed 2026-08-17: 'less text at the top of admin') one-line intro, the top disclosure that now covers EVERY
site (id=permission-map + its body mount), and the four role filters collapsed into one symmetric
'Role, per site' section.
mustNotContain pins the REMOVAL half, per the rework precedent: the old single-site ladder
(id=role-ladder, 'Audiobooks/Ebooks role ladder') and the old per-site filter wording ('Site role
(both shelves)') are exactly what a stale bundle would still carry while serving a cheerful 200 and
satisfying every mustContain. The two older removals ('>Audiobook' and 'Audiobook role
ladder', from the 2026-08-17 row merge) are kept — they cost nothing and still pin real removals.
⚠️ THE THREE-SECTION DIRECTORY (2026-08-17, owner: 'i revoked access to an account on /admin, its
still in the list, lets move these to a revoked section, lets also make the effort to have a pending
area too while we're in here. make pending, revoked, and current members list all collapsable'). The
SECTIONS themselves are drawn by admin.js after sign-in and are pinned in that file's entry below;
what ships in this HTML and is assertable unauthenticated is the shape they need — the intro that
states the page has three lists, and the .dir-group/.dir-empty/.users-list CSS the sections are built
from. The removal half is the one that matters most here and is a single string: the directory mount
was '<ul id="users"' and is now a <div>, because a <details> is not a legal child of a list. A stale
bundle serving the old <ul> would render three sections into an invalid tree and still return 200.
admin.js — ONE entry since 2026-08-17 (it was two, both fetching the same file: the library2
federation and the ebook gate. One file, one marker set, one place to look).
Everything this page RENDERS is injected only after Firebase sign-in, so what CAN be asserted
unauthenticated is the module's own anatomy — and after the control-grammar reshape that anatomy is
exactly what changed: SITE_ROWS is the one row list that drives the per-member grid, the top
permission map and the filter order; pendingEdits + savePermissions + 'Save permissions' +
perm-staged are the stage-then-Save grammar that replaced four different commit gestures;
RUNG_MEANINGS is the derived capability column; renderPermissionMap is the every-site ladder.
padhard.heygabi.ai/library2/ROLE_FILTER_KEYS keep proving all four sites are federated at all, and
MERGED_ROW keeps proving f7697f4's merged Audiobooks/Ebooks row survived the reshape (now as one
grid row with two boxes).
⚠️ THE DOWNLOAD FACT SWAPPED SIDES THE SAME DAY, and the markers swapped with it. The owner saw the
standalone tag live and killed it: 'what is this download: admin + role tag it looks bad and idk
what its trying to tell me.' So 'downloadNoteCell' and 'download: admin+ role' moved from
mustContain to mustNotContain, and what is asserted instead is where the fact went —
EBOOK_DOWNLOAD_RUNG (the documented admin floor) and the sentence the derived capability line now
appends, 'Includes downloading ebook files.' Asserting the old strings would now be exactly
backwards, which is the same trap this file already hit twice on 2026-08-16/17.
⚠️ mustNotContain pins SEVEN killed idioms, each naming a specific way the page used to disagree
with itself: saveVisibility wrote a checkbox the instant it was ticked; the one-tap button helper
(actionBtn) made Approve the only status action that did not confirm; 'Set role' was the two-tap
apply button that ONLY the audiobook row had; renderRoleTree drew a ladder for that one site and
nothing for the other three; cat-vis is the old row layout the grid replaced; downloadNoteCell and
its tag text are the note the owner rejected. A bundle still carrying any of them is a bundle still
shipping the divergence he asked to remove, and it would pass every mustContain above. The four
2026-08-17 download-rework removals are kept for the same reason they were added.
⚠️ THE THREE-SECTION DIRECTORY (2026-08-17). The sections ARE this module — the HTML ships only an
empty mount — so these are the markers that prove the reshape landed rather than the shell around it.
DIRECTORY_GROUPS is the one list that names the three statuses and their defaults; directorySection is
the builder; openGroups is what stops a search keystroke or a mutation re-render slamming a section
the reader opened; 'Current members' is the section header the owner asked for by name; 'Nobody is
waiting.' is the worded empty state (his standing rule: never a bare empty box); and 'hidden by the
current search or filters' is the OTHER empty state — the one that must never be confused with the
first, since printing 'nobody is waiting' while a filter hides a pending person says the opposite of
the truth. A bundle missing any of these renders a flat list again and returns a cheerful 200.
NOTE (unchanged, and the reason this file's checks can never be enough): the signed-in rendered
table — the grid, the Save, the ladders with real data, and now the three sections themselves — is
invisible to an unauthenticated fetch and still has to be checked by signing in.
mustContain: hidden by the current search or filters
mustNotContain: download: admin on the audiobook role above

_why: /docs (2026-08-18, GABI docs assistant phase 6) is a GATED page and, unusually, a CONTENT-FREE one:
every heading, path, snippet and section body arrives from auth.heygabi.ai behind requireDevops(),
so an unauthenticated fetch can only ever see the shell. That is the point — view the source signed
out and there is no documentation here. So the markers are the SHELL and its GATE, and each is a
piece whose absence would leave a page that still returns a cheerful 200 while doing nothing:
id=q is the search input the owner asked for by name ('make it with a search bar'), id=results is
where hits land, id=snapstrip is the always-visible publish date (a docs page that looks equally
confident when it is nine days behind is worse than none), id=reader/id=reader-body are the section
view, and id=signin plus the worded gate line are the signed-out state — never a blank.
⚠️ The gate line is asserted as TEXT, not only as an element: a bundle that shipped the markup with
an empty gate would satisfy an id-only marker and still show a person a bare box.
docs.js — everything this page DOES lives here, and none of it is visible to an unauthenticated
fetch, so the markers are the module's own anatomy. Each names a decision a stale bundle would
silently lose: the two Worker routes (a page still pointing at the old KV /:slug endpoint would 404
forever and read as 'no docs published'), markText is the result highlighting, renderMarkdown is the
rendered section view, describeFailure is the one place an HTTP outcome becomes a sentence, and
'not your permissions' is the outage wording that must never collapse back into a permission
refusal — the estate's standing rule, and the row most easily mislabelled.
⚠️ mustNotContain pins the one thing this renderer must never acquire. Every node is built with
textContent precisely because the corpus is full of angle brackets in shell one-liners and <script>
inside code fences; an innerHTML assignment reappearing here would either execute those or silently
eat them, and would pass every mustContain above.
/series (2026-08-17) is a GATED page: /api/series and /api/series/:slug both sit below the index
Worker's requireEstateMember() blanket, so every series row, every volume and every gap row is
injected only after a Firebase sign-in this unauthenticated fetch never has. What CAN be asserted
here is the SHELL and its gate: the heading, the back arrow, the ids the script fills, and the
sign-in button that is the signed-out state's whole content. The volume view itself, including the
gap rows, has to be checked by signing in — said plainly rather than implied by a green check.
ser-pending (2026-08-18) is the confirm-queue banner's EMPTY SHELL — the markup ships hidden and is
filled only when GET /api/series answers with pending_detail, which the Worker sends to approvers
alone. So this marker proves the container shipped and nothing more; whether the banner SPEAKS can
only be checked signed in as an approver with a row open in the queue.
The page's whole behaviour lives in this module, so the markers are the three things whose absence
would mean it shipped without its reason to exist: the gap sentence the owner asked for, the
source→household vocabulary that names who holds a volume, and the detail endpoint it expands with.
pending_detail (2026-08-18) is the fourth: it is the ONLY thing that makes the confirm-queue banner
appear, and it is read from the list answer rather than decided here. A bundle that shipped without
it would show an approver a clean page while a decision sat unresolved — the exact silence the field
was added to end.
mustContain: nobody in the estate has this one
